summary:
The Solar Orbiter TM-TC and Packet Structure Interface Control Document (SOL.S.ASTR.TN.00079, issue 7), written by Airbus Defence and Space for ESA and generated from its DOORS requirements database. It is the baseline definition of the structure and syntax of all application-level TM/TC traffic between the on-board computer, the solid-state mass memory, the ten payload instruments and the star trackers, based on PUS-A (ECSS-E-70-41A).

Chapters 3 and 4 define the packet and frame layers as used on the spacecraft: the TC source packet (7-bit process ID plus category 12, at most 242 octets of data field, PUS version 1 header, CRC), TC segments (MAP ID 0 for CPDU high-priority commands and 1 for normal commands, packet aggregation without segmentation), the TC transfer frame (spacecraft ID 0x28A = 650, VC 1 and 2 for the two decoders, a maximum frame length of 256 octets, AD/BD/BC frame types); the TM source packet (up to 4112 octets, 10-octet data field header with CUC 4+2 time) and the TM transfer frame (1115 octets, VC usage and priority, CLCW in every frame, a 3-octet secondary header extending the VC frame count).

Chapter 5, the bulk of the document, lists every service and subservice tailored for Solar Orbiter (standard services 1 to 22 and private services such as 130 TM extraction, 133 file management, 134 TC sequencer, 139 parameter management and 142 functional monitoring), with packet layouts and parameter definitions, and which unit must implement each. Annexes define bit numbering, field alignment, the time and idle packets, the CRC algorithm with test vectors, the APID/category/process ID allocation, source and destination IDs, failure and event IDs and service 3 SIDs. It is the primary reference for decoding real Solar Orbiter packets against the MIB.

key_points.text: The ICD is the baseline definition of all application-level TM/TC data structures on board Solar Orbiter (OBC, SSMM, 10 payload instruments, star tracker), based on ECSS-E-70-41A; non-standard use of standardised PUS services is forbidden and user-specific packets must be private services.
TC APID = 7-bit Process ID plus 4-bit Packet Category fixed to decimal 12; sequence flags are always 11 (stand-alone); the sequence count is kept per APID and Source ID and is not checked on board.
The maximum TC packet data field is 242 octets: 4 octets data field header, 236 octets application data and 2 octets packet error control.
In the TC data field header the PUS version is 1; only the acceptance (bit 3) and completion (bit 0) acknowledgement flags are used, with start and progress set to zero.
TC segments are never segmented (sequence flags 11); MAP ID 0 is for CPDU commands TC(2,3) and MAP ID 1 for normal commands, and several packets may be aggregated in one segment.
The CCSDS spacecraft ID is 0x28A (650) for TM and TC; TC virtual channels 1 and 2 address the two on-board decoders, and the maximum TC frame length is 256 octets.
The maximum TM source packet is 4112 octets; packets longer than the 1099-octet frame data field are spread over frames. APID 0 is reserved for the time packet and all ones for idle packets.

The TM source sequence count is maintained per APID and Destination ID, and the TM data field is at most 4106 octets (10 octets header plus 4096 source data); packet time uses CUC with 4 coarse and 2 fine octets.
The only allowed TM frame length is 1115 octets; every frame carries a CLCW in the OCF and a secondary header with a 3-octet extension of the VC frame count (secondary header ID 0b00000011).

Downlink priority is VC4 real-time high priority, VC5 critical event log, VC0 real time, VC1 OBC mass memory playback, VC2 and VC3 SSMM playback, and VC7 idle frames; only VC2 and VC3 may contain compressed packets.

The standard spacecraft time packet has APID 0, no data field header, 8 octets of data (C=7) with P-field 0b00101110 (4+2 CUC), and its time refers to the leading edge of the ASM of VC0 frame count 0.
The packet error control CRC uses G(x) = x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1 with the register initialised to all ones; test vectors include 00 00 -> 1D0F and AB CD EF 01 -> 04A2.

Packet categories: 0 time, 1 TC verification, 2 high-priority TM, 3 tables, 4 routine HK, 5 functional cyclic, 6 functional non-cyclic, 7 events, 8 diagnostic, 9 dump, 10 file transfer, 11 context, 12 science or TC, 15 idle.

Process IDs: 10 to 16 OBC CSW applications (DMS, AOCS, payload, platform, system control, OBCP, thermal), 30 to 32 SSMM, 40/41 star trackers, 49 payload broadcast, 50 to 104 instruments (for example SWA 95 to 99), 112 to 127 EGSE.
Ground source IDs are 110 mission timeline, 111 TC sequences, 112 recovery actions, 113 backup mission timeline and 120 direct commands; on-board sources are 15 OBCP, 14 system control and 11 AOCS.

notes: The cover (PDF p. 1) is a scanned signature page; its OCR text is garbled ('lCD' for 'ICD', handwritten names and dates unreadable), so the issue date is not legible and is recorded as null. Legible fragments name the checkers K. Smith (SW Architect) and S. Brady (DB Architect) and the PA manager T. Hunt; the PDF metadata creation date is 28 November 2014 and the copyright year 2014. PDF page indices equal printed page numbers (Page N of 396); the extracted text has an empty 397th page. Numbers at the right margin of the text (e.g. 'PUS-31//', '13902') are DOORS object identifiers, not page numbers. Many packet layout figures are images and have no text. PDF pp. 283-294 hold the issue change record and distribution list; PDF pp. 295-395 are an auto-generated DOORS change log, which states that the main body takes precedence. The file was retrieved from the IRAP Solar Orbiter document server; it is marked as supplied in confidence by Airbus, so only facts are paraphrased here. Issue 6 of this ICD is the [RD 01] of sol-sgs-tn-0007-s20-2-0.
